items.title: Catalog entry build_dependencies does not match EXTENSION_DEPENDS in CMakeLists.txt

findings.title: Catalog entry build_dependencies does not match EXTENSION_DEPENDS in CMakeLists.txt
findings.evidence:
# PyTorch and NNUNet extensions supply PyTorchUtils and SlicerNNUNetLib used by setupPythonRequirements().
set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "PyTorch NNUNet")
findings.explanation: The extension's CMakeLists.txt declares EXTENSION_DEPENDS "PyTorch NNUNet" (and the repository's own SeqSeg.json has "build_dependencies": ["PyTorch", "NNUNet"]), whereas the catalog entry in the ExtensionsIndex PR has "build_dependencies": []. They must match so the extension manager and build system know about the required PyTorch and NNUNet extensions.
findings.suggestion: Update the catalog entry in the ExtensionsIndex PR to set "build_dependencies": ["PyTorch", "NNUNet"] (matching CMakeLists.txt and SeqSeg.json in the repository).

findings.title: Catalog omits the build dependencies declared by the extension
findings.evidence:
# PyTorch and NNUNet extensions supply PyTorchUtils and SlicerNNUNetLib used by setupPythonRequirements().
set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "PyTorch NNUNet")
findings.explanation: The submitted index entry in the request has an empty build_dependencies array, although CMake declares both dependencies and runtime setup imports their libraries. The index cannot schedule or install those prerequisites from the submitted metadata. The separate SeqSeg.json in the source repository does list them, but it is not the submitted index entry.
findings.suggestion: Set the index entry's build_dependencies to ["PyTorch", "NNUNet"] and verify the index resolves them.

claude.reason: CMakeLists.txt:13 has set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "PyTorch NNUNet") and the repo's SeqSeg.json:3 has ["PyTorch","NNUNet"], and seqseg.py:1973,1990 import PyTorchUtils and SlicerNNUNetLib. I can't see the ExtensionsIndex entry itself, so I can't confirm that it has an empty build_dependencies array. If it is empty, that is a real mismatch and the dependency extensions wouldn't be built or installed. Metadata mismatches are fixable and the module fails with a clear InstallError (1975-1981, 1992-1998). Major if confirmed, not blocking.

gpt.reason: CMakeLists.txt:12-13 says `# PyTorch and NNUNet extensions supply PyTorchUtils and SlicerNNUNetLib used by setupPythonRequirements().` and `set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "PyTorch NNUNet")`. The only catalog entry available to inspect is the source repository's SeqSeg.json:3, `"build_dependencies": ["PyTorch", "NNUNet"],`, which matches. The separate submitted index entry and its claimed empty array are not available through these tools, so a mismatch and its build impact cannot be independently verified. Exact checked-out revision is also not independently verifiable.

gemini.reason: CMakeLists.txt lines 12-13 sets `EXTENSION_DEPENDS "PyTorch NNUNet"` (and the repository's own `SeqSeg.json` line 3 has `"build_dependencies": ["PyTorch", "NNUNet"]`). If the catalog entry in the ExtensionsIndex PR has `"build_dependencies": []`, it does not match `EXTENSION_DEPENDS` and the Extension Manager will not install the required PyTorch and NNUNet extensions. Under the rubric ("EXTENSION_DEPENDS matches the entry's build_dependencies"), this is a blocking packaging issue.

findings.title: Running segmentation overwrites existing seeds and input images
findings.evidence:

            with open(seeds_file, 'w') as f:
                json.dump(seeds_data, f, indent=4)
findings.explanation: Each run truncates any existing seeds.json in the chosen output directory without asking, including a user-maintained file unrelated to this run. Lines 2434–2438 likewise save the input volume to a predictable images/<sanitized-volume-name>.nii.gz, potentially replacing a previous image with the same name.
findings.suggestion: Create a unique per-run workspace, or detect collisions and request explicit overwrite permission before writing any input or seed file.

claude.reason: seqseg.py:2465-2467 writes seeds.json with open(...,'w'), and 2437-2438 saves images/<name>.nii.gz, both in the output directory the user chose for this run. They are the module's own working files, so overwriting them on re-run is expected. It is a convenience issue, not a concrete path to harm, and not blocking.

gpt.reason: seqseg/seqseg.py:2423-2424 uses `data_dir = outputDirectory`; lines 2465-2467 say `seeds_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "seeds.json")`, `with open(seeds_file, 'w') as f:`, `json.dump(seeds_data, f, indent=4)`. An existing unrelated seeds.json is truncated without an overwrite confirmation, potentially losing user data. Lines 2434-2438 additionally derive `input_file = os.path.join(images_dir, f"{case_name}.nii.gz")` and call `slicer.util.saveNode(inputVolume, input_file)`, risking a collision with an existing image; actual Slicer save behavior was not run. The output path may also default to ~/SeqSeg_Output (lines 461-467).

gemini.reason: In `seqseg/seqseg.py` lines 2437-2438 and 2465-2467, running segmentation writes `images/<case_name>.nii.gz` and `seeds.json` inside the user-selected `outputDirectory`. Because `outputDirectory` is specifically chosen by the user in the UI as the working/output directory for the SeqSeg run (and SeqSeg requires this directory structure), writing the run's input image and seed file there is expected behavior, though overwriting without a prompt if a user reuses a directory is a minor usability/soundness detail rather than a blocking safety issue.

items.title: SeqSeg and its dependencies install or upgrade without confirmation

findings.title: seqseg PyPI package is installed or upgraded without user confirmation when PyTorch and nnUNet are already present
findings.evidence:
seqseg_install_command = self._seqseg_install_command(installed_seqseg_version, upgrade=upgrade)
        if seqseg_install_command:
            logging.info(_("Installing SeqSeg Python package ({spec})...").format(spec=seqseg_install_command))
            self.pipInstallSelective(self.SEQSEG_PYTHON_PACKAGE_NAME, seqseg_install_command, packagesToSkip)
findings.explanation: If `PyTorch` and `nnunetv2` are already installed, `confirmPackagesToInstall` is empty so `slicer.util.confirmOkCancelDisplay` is skipped, yet `setupPythonRequirements()` still proceeds to query PyPI and run `pipInstallSelective` to install or upgrade `seqseg` and its transitive dependencies (`vtk`, `scipy`, `matplotlib`, etc., if any are declared by `seqseg` and not in `packagesToSkip`) without asking the user first. Furthermore, `packagesToSkip` omits `vtk` and `scipy` which Slicer bundles.
findings.suggestion: Include `seqseg` in `confirmPackagesToInstall` so the user is always prompted before installing or upgrading `seqseg` from PyPI, and add `vtk`, `scipy`, and `pydicom` to `packagesToSkip` so `seqseg`'s dependencies cannot overwrite Slicer's bundled packages.

findings.evidence:

findings.explanation: The earlier confirmation only lists missing or mismatched PyTorch and nnunetv2. When those are already present, the first run installs SeqSeg and its selectively processed dependencies without a dialog; later runs automatically upgrade to the current PyPI release, also without confirmation. This can download substantial packages and change the shared environment unexpectedly.
findings.suggestion: Include SeqSeg and all planned dependency installations and upgrades in an explicit confirmation before changing the environment; avoid automatically upgrading on every run.

claude.reason: seqseg.py:2008-2016 only prompts for PyTorch and nnunetv2. The seqseg install at 2072-2075 and the pipInstallSelective dependency installs at 1855 run without confirmation, and they query PyPI at 1864. This happens only after the user explicitly starts a segmentation, which is the module's purpose. packagesToSkip (1960-1968) omits vtk and scipy, so a pip dependency could touch them. The lack of a prompt and the PyPI lookup are worth improving but are not blocking.

gpt.reason: seqseg/seqseg.py:2008-2014 only displays confirmation if `confirmPackagesToInstall` is nonempty, and lists that array; lines 1983-1987 and 2003-2006 only add PyTorch and nnunetv2. Lines 2072-2075 then call `self.pipInstallSelective(self.SEQSEG_PYTHON_PACKAGE_NAME, seqseg_install_command, packagesToSkip)` regardless of whether SeqSeg was mentioned or confirmation shown. Lines 1890-1900 select installation if absent or upgrade when PyPI has a newer version; lines 1851-1855 install remaining requirements. This can modify the shared environment without informed confirmation. VTK/scipy are not in the skip list at lines 1960-1968, but the actual external package requirements and download sizes were not available to verify.

gemini.reason: In `seqseg/seqseg.py` lines 1970-2016 and 2072-2075, `confirmPackagesToInstall` only checks `PyTorch` and `nnunetv2`. If those are already installed, `confirmOkCancelDisplay` is skipped, and `setupPythonRequirements()` proceeds to query PyPI (`_latest_pypi_version`, lines 1859-1873) and run `pipInstallSelective` to install or upgrade `seqseg` and its non-skipped dependencies (`vtk`, `scipy`, etc. are not in `packagesToSkip` at lines 1960-1968) without user confirmation. items.title: Unprompted downgrade of Slicer's bundled NumPy (`numpy<2`) and exact pin of PyTorch 2.2.2

findings.title: Unprompted downgrade of Slicer's bundled NumPy (`numpy<2`) and exact pin of PyTorch 2.2.2
findings.evidence:
numpy_version_str = importlib.metadata.version("numpy")
        if pkg_version.parse(numpy_version_str) >= pkg_version.parse("2.0.0"):
            logging.info(_("Downgrading NumPy from {current} to <2 for PyTorch 2.2.2 compatibility...").format(current=numpy_version_str))
            slicer.util.pip_install("numpy<2")
            raise InstallError(
                _("NumPy 2.x is incompatible with the required PyTorch 2.2.2. NumPy was downgraded to 1.x; restart Slicer and run SeqSeg again."),
                restartRequired=True,
            )
findings.explanation: When the user runs SeqSeg, setupPythonRequirements() checks if numpy >= 2.0.0 and immediately runs `slicer.util.pip_install("numpy<2")` without user confirmation (before `confirmOkCancelDisplay` is ever reached), and additionally forces an exact pin of `torch==2.2.2` and `torchvision==0.17.2` (lines 1941-1942, 2022-2023). Downgrading Slicer's bundled numpy or overriding already-installed PyTorch/nnUNet versions modifies Slicer's shared Python environment and can break Slicer core or other installed extensions (such as TotalSegmentator or MONAI) that rely on Slicer's bundled numpy or a newer PyTorch build.
findings.suggestion: Do not downgrade Slicer's bundled `numpy` package or force-pin `torch==2.2.2`. Instead, allow `PyTorchUtils` and `SlicerNNUNetLib` to use or install versions compatible with the current Slicer release, and ensure all package installations only happen after explicit user confirmation.

findings.explanation: On a Slicer installation with NumPy 2, starting a run immediately replaces the shared package before the dependency confirmation or even checking that required extensions are present. This can break Slicer or unrelated extensions after restart.
findings.suggestion: Support the Slicer-provided NumPy and a compatible PyTorch version rather than downgrading the shared environment.

claude.reason: seqseg.py:1951-1958 runs slicer.util.pip_install("numpy<2") with no confirmation when NumPy is 2.x. It runs before the extension checks and before the confirm dialog at 2009. It then forces a restart. This downgrades a package Slicer bundles in the shared environment and could affect other extensions. The code logs the change and shows an error telling the user to restart, and it triggers only on an explicit user run. Major under the environment policy, not blocking.

gpt.reason: seqseg/seqseg.py:1951-1954 says `numpy_version_str = importlib.metadata.version("numpy")`, `if pkg_version.parse(numpy_version_str) >= pkg_version.parse("2.0.0"):`, then `slicer.util.pip_install("numpy<2")`. This runs on a segmentation attempt (line 2421) before the confirmation at lines 2008-2015 and before dependency-extension checks, replacing Slicer's shared NumPy for NumPy 2 users and risking breakage. Lines 1941-1942 set exact torch and torchvision versions and lines 2020-2023 pass them to the PyTorch extension after a generic confirmation. Unlike NumPy, the torch change is not entirely unprompted; actual installation depends on the external extension.

gemini.reason: In `seqseg/seqseg.py` lines 1951-1958, at the very beginning of `setupPythonRequirements()`, before any user confirmation dialog (`confirmOkCancelDisplay` at line 2009), the code checks if `numpy >= 2.0.0` and immediately executes `slicer.util.pip_install("numpy<2")`. Furthermore, lines 1941-1942 and 2020-2023 force an exact pin `torch==2.2.2` and `torchvision==0.17.2`. Under the review policy and rubric, downgrading Slicer's bundled packages (like numpy) or forcing exact pins without confirmation in Slicer's shared Python environment can break Slicer and other extensions and is a blocking environment issue.

items.title: Weight download overwrites and deletes an existing archive

findings.title: Weight archive extraction uses zipfile.extractall without checksum verification or member path validation
findings.evidence:
logging.info(f"Extracting {zip_file} to {download_dir}")
                with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_file, 'r') as zip_ref:
                    zip_ref.extractall(download_dir)
findings.explanation: `_downloadNnunetWeightsFromZenodo` downloads a zip archive over HTTPS from fixed Zenodo record URLs and extracts it with `zip_ref.extractall(download_dir)` without verifying a cryptographic checksum (unlike `SampleData`) or validating archive member paths against path traversal (`..`). While the Zenodo URLs are hardcoded, verifying SHA256 checksums and validating zip member paths before extraction is safer practice.
findings.suggestion: Verify the SHA256 checksum of the downloaded `.zip` archive before extracting, and validate that all member paths in the `ZipFile` resolve inside `download_dir` before extraction.

findings.title: Weight download overwrites and deletes an existing archive
findings.evidence:
logging.info(f"Extracting {zip_file} to {download_dir}")
                with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_file, 'r') as zip_ref:
                    zip_ref.extractall(download_dir)

                os.remove(zip_file)
findings.explanation: The archive is downloaded to a fixed filename in the directory chosen by the user, and urlretrieve at line 1542 overwrites that file before it is deleted here. The existing-weights prompt only tests the extracted directory, so an unrelated nnUNet_results.zip or nnUNet_results_coronary.zip can be destroyed without warning. Extraction can also overwrite existing files in the destination.
findings.suggestion: Download to a unique temporary file, extract to a new staging directory, and handle destination collisions explicitly before moving results into place.

claude.reason: seqseg.py:1531 and 1542 use urlretrieve to write a fixed-name zip in the user-chosen directory, which overwrites an existing file of that name. Line 1551 then removes it. Line 1549 calls extractall from a fixed Zenodo URL. The existing-weights prompt (1505-1510) covers only the extracted folder. There is no checksum, but Python's zipfile strips '..' components. The risk is limited to a file of the module's own weights-archive name, so it is minor.

gpt.reason: seqseg/seqseg.py:1531-1542 constructs `zip_file = os.path.join(download_dir, zip_filename)` and calls `urllib.request.urlretrieve(zenodo_file_url, zip_file, show_progress)`; lines 1547-1551 extract it and call `os.remove(zip_file)`. The overwrite prompt at lines 1504-1510 checks only the extracted directory, not an existing archive. A user choosing a directory containing an unrelated file of the fixed name at lines 1389-1403 can lose that file without warning. Extraction can also overwrite colliding members. No checksum is checked in the shown download path; lack of a separate member-path validation is not, by itself, proof of exploitable traversal because Python's zipfile sanitizes ordinary traversal names. Archive contents were not inspected.

gemini.reason: In `seqseg/seqseg.py` lines 1483-1551, the user explicitly clicks a download button and selects `download_dir` via a file dialog (`Select directory to download model weights`), is prompted if `weights_path` already exists (lines 1505-1509), and then the Zenodo zip archive is downloaded to `zip_file`, extracted with `extractall(download_dir)`, and the temporary `zip_file` is removed (`os.remove(zip_file)`). Since the URLs are fixed HTTPS Zenodo records and the user explicitly initiates the download into a chosen folder, lack of SHA256 verification / zip member validation / temporary zip overwrite is a minor issue, not a blocking safety flaw.

findings.title: Existing shared PyTorch is forced to an old exact version
findings.evidence:
if "PyTorch" in confirmPackagesToInstall:
            logging.info(_("Installing PyTorch Python packages (may take several minutes)..."))
            torch_result = torchLogic.installTorch(
                askConfirmation=False,
                torchVersionRequirement=f"=={requiredTorchVersion}",
                torchVisionVersionRequirement=f"=={requiredTorchVisionVersion}",
findings.explanation: Any installed torch version whose base version is not 2.2.2 is treated as requiring replacement, including newer versions used by other extensions. Although the PyTorch extension performs the install and a generic confirmation is shown, users are not told that an existing shared installation may be downgraded.
findings.suggestion: Support compatible installed PyTorch versions and avoid forcing a shared exact version; if replacement is unavoidable, clearly disclose the current and proposed versions.

claude.reason: seqseg.py:1941-1942 pin torch 2.2.2 and torchvision 0.17.2. Lines 1986-1987 flag any other torch version for replacement, and 2020-2023 install the exact pins through PyTorchUtils. The dialog at 2010-2014 only says PyTorch will be installed and does not mention a downgrade. The rubric asks for changes on exact torch pins, and this can replace a newer shared torch. It goes through the PyTorch extension and a confirmation is shown, so it is major, not blocking.

gpt.reason: seqseg/seqseg.py:1941-1947 defines `requiredTorchVersion = "2.2.2"` and compares installed base versions against it. Lines 1983-1987 add `PyTorch` to the installation list for any mismatch; lines 2018-2023 call `torchLogic.installTorch(` with `askConfirmation=False`, `torchVersionRequirement=f"=={requiredTorchVersion}"`, and the exact torchvision requirement. The generic prior prompt at lines 2008-2014 does not describe a downgrade or version replacement. This requests replacement of a newer shared torch; the external PyTorch extension's success and exact behavior were not verified.

gemini.reason: In `seqseg/seqseg.py` lines 1941, 1946-1947, 1986-1987, and 2018-2023, any installed PyTorch version whose base version is not exactly `2.2.2` is added to `confirmPackagesToInstall` and replaced via `torchLogic.installTorch(..., torchVersionRequirement="==2.2.2", torchVisionVersionRequirement="==0.17.2")`. The confirmation dialog (lines 2009-2014) only says PyTorch will be installed, without warning that a newer existing PyTorch installation shared with other extensions will be downgraded to 2.2.2.

items.title: Running `seqseg` CLI via bare executable name in synchronous subprocess.run

findings.title: Running `seqseg` CLI via bare executable name in synchronous subprocess.run
findings.evidence:
def _run_seqseg_cli(self, seqseg_cmd, cwd):
        logging.info(f"Running SeqSeg command: {' '.join(seqseg_cmd)}")
        result = subprocess.run(
            seqseg_cmd,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            cwd=cwd,
        )
findings.explanation: `subprocess.run(["seqseg", ...])` is called synchronously on the main UI thread, freezing the Slicer GUI while nnUNet inference runs, and relies on `"seqseg"` being on the system `PATH`. On some platforms (especially Windows or macOS app bundles), Slicer's Python scripts directory is not necessarily on `PATH`, so invoking `seqseg` by bare executable name can fail with `FileNotFoundError` even when the `seqseg` package is installed in Slicer's Python environment.
findings.suggestion: Invoke SeqSeg via `sys.executable` (e.g., `[sys.executable, "-m", "seqseg", ...]` or resolving the script path inside Slicer's Python `bin`/`Scripts` folder) so it reliably uses Slicer's Python environment.

items.title: Tutorial describes seed controls that no longer match the module

findings.title: Tutorial describes seed controls that no longer match the module
findings.evidence:
After the volume is in Slicer, open **SeqSeg Vessel Segmentation**, click **Auto-Create Seeds**, then **toggle on Planes visible in 3D** for the seed markups (so slice intersections show in the 3D view). Zoom into the anatomy and **drag the seed points** until they sit where you want (inside the vessel).

Whether you used **Auto-Create Seeds** or the **Markups** module, you need two fiducials in the vessel. Place **Seed point 1** in the **ascending aorta** near the **aortic root / proximal ascending** segment, and **Seed point 2** **higher** along the same lumen toward the **arch**—both inside the contrast-filled vessel. Seed 1 is the start; seed 2 sets the initial tracking direction along the aorta.
findings.explanation: The inspected UI instead provides Add Seed for tagged two-point line markups, and the implementation collects tagged line nodes rather than arbitrary fiducials. Users following the tutorial cannot perform the described steps as written.
findings.suggestion: Update the tutorial and screenshots to explain Add Seed, line placement and the radius derived from line length.

Instead, allow `PyTorchUtils` and `SlicerNNUNetLib` to use or install versions compatible with the current Slicer release, and ensure all package installations only happen after explicit user confirmation.
